payload.verdict: A software engineering graduate with useful projects, but an internship that leaves too much of the work unnamed.
write_up: Your resume points to entry-level Software Engineer work: a computer science degree, a Meridian Health Supply internship and several application projects. It's common for an internship resume to lean on duties, but your recent lines mostly leave the features, tests and fixes unnamed. That makes it difficult to stand out alongside other graduates who list the same tools.

The Personal Finance Tracker line is a good model: it names the application, what it does and the tools you used. Your help desk and internship experience can lead the resume, so put Experience above Education. The objective names the job you want, but its general claims take space that could show your engineering work.

Let's start with the Meridian internship. Name a feature you developed, a test you wrote and a bug you fixed, sticking to what you can describe accurately. Then use the same approach for the help desk work and keep the project details that show what you built.

cards.line: Motivated and detail-oriented Computer Science graduate seeking a Software Engineer position where I can leverage my technical skills and passion for problem solving to contribute to a dynamic team.
cards.cannot_tell: The job you want is clear, but the rest could describe almost any graduate. Put your inventory application work up front instead.
cards.example: Computer Science graduate seeking a Software Engineer position, with experience developing [feature] for an internal inventory management web application using React and Spring Boot
cards.question: Which feature did you develop for the inventory application?

cards.cannot_tell: Your help desk and internship work give a recruiter something to look at before coursework. Move Experience above Education so that work comes first.
cards.question: Can you move Experience above Education?

cards.line: Meridian Health Supply isn't described beyond its name and location.
cards.cannot_tell: A short description of the employer could give a recruiter context for the inventory application, if it adds something the name doesn't already say.
cards.example: Meridian Health Supply: [what the employer does] for [customers]
cards.question: What does Meridian Health Supply do, and who does it serve?

cards.line: Soft Skills: Communication, Teamwork, Leadership, Time Management, Problem Solving
cards.cannot_tell: These claims don't show how you used those skills. Consider trimming the list and giving that space to a concrete example from your work.
cards.example: [What you did] for [project or team], resulting in [what changed]
cards.question: What did you do on a project or team, and what changed as a result?

cards.line: Responsible for developing features for an internal inventory management web application using React and Spring Boot
cards.cannot_tell: The application and tools are named, but the features aren't. A recruiter can't tell what part of the inventory application you developed.
cards.example: Developed [feature] for an internal inventory management web application using React and Spring Boot
cards.question: Which feature did you develop for the application?

cards.line: Participated in daily stand-ups and sprint planning meetings as part of an Agile team
cards.cannot_tell: Meetings were part of the job, but this doesn't show what you contributed. If there's a concrete planning contribution, name it; otherwise, use the room for your development work.
cards.example: Participated in sprint planning meetings for [project], contributing [planning contribution]
cards.question: What did you contribute to planning for the team's work?

cards.line: Wrote unit tests to improve code quality and reliability
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see that you wrote tests, but not what you tested. Naming the feature or behavior would connect this to your engineering work.
cards.example: Wrote unit tests for [feature or behavior] using [test tool]
cards.question: What did you test, and what tool did you use?

cards.line: Collaborated with cross-functional teams to gather requirements and deliver solutions
cards.cannot_tell: The teams, requirements and solutions are all unnamed. Pick one piece of work and show your part in it.
cards.example: Collaborated with [team] to gather requirements for [feature] and deliver [your contribution]
cards.question: Which team did you work with, and what did you contribute to a feature or solution?

cards.line: Fixed bugs and performed code reviews
cards.cannot_tell: Both are useful engineering tasks, but neither has an example attached. A bug you fixed or a review you contributed to would give a recruiter more to discuss.
cards.example: Fixed [bug] in [feature] and performed code reviews for [work reviewed]
cards.question: What bug did you fix, and what work did you review?

cards.line: Provided technical support to students and faculty for hardware and software issues
cards.cannot_tell: The people you supported are clear, but the problems are broad. Name an issue you handled and, if you know it, how many requests you supported.
cards.example: Provided technical support to students and faculty for [issue], handling [number] requests [time period]
cards.question: What kind of issue did you handle, and how many requests did you support in a typical period?

cards.line: Resolved tickets in a timely manner and documented solutions
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can't tell what the tickets involved or what you documented. One example would show the work behind the tickets.
cards.question: What was one issue you resolved and documented?

cards.line: Assisted with setting up laptops and classroom technology
cards.cannot_tell: Assisted can cover several different tasks. Say what part of the setup was yours.
cards.example: Assisted with setting up laptops and classroom technology by [your setup task]
cards.question: What did you do when setting up the laptops or classroom technology?

fit.why: Your objective names Software Engineer, and your internship and projects show application development work.
fit.level: entry level, a software engineering internship and a computer science degree
fit.note: Your React and Spring Boot internship and full-stack capstone point toward application development roles. The Python and JavaScript projects give you more work to discuss alongside the internship.
